admission.justification: The fake runtime exposes the usage port so the controlled recurring-owner cases reach their unchanged per-stage attribution and repeated-cancel assertions.

applicability: The controlled recurring-owner accounting proof, including its held-delivery owner.
conditions: The fake serving runtime supplies usage_read=None as the real runtime does.
Existing success, failure-at-stage and repeated-cancellation assertions remain.
exclusions: No native-host or broad performance acceptance.

evidence: evidence/items2-4-before.log 3 failed on base bytes (SUBFAILED owner='held' success, failure and cancel); evidence/items2-4-after.log 1 passed with 30 subtests passed on the candidate; the case arrived with 87992ce842079a7a4f161bd4bfcc4aed5307178b (L81) and the runtime contract usage_read with 1ef442f478a118031599a90f9b547adca503d595 (L184)

statement: The proof's fake serving runtime carries usage_read with the real _ServingRuntime's None default, so the held-delivery sweep runs and every recurring owner attributes each stage and drains a repeated cancel.
